items.title: The 'quite terrifying' scenarios that finally spooked global markets
items.description: For more than a year, traders have been pushing markets higher on the hopes of an AI-powered economic miracle and the notion of TACO — Trump Always Chickens Out. Now it looks like the penny has dropped.

items.title: Breaking: Five Iranian women's soccer players to seek asylum in Australia, multiple sources say
items.description: Five female soccer players who it was feared would face persecution when they returned to Iran have left their accommodation in the Gold Coast and plan to seek asylum in Australia, multiple sources have told the ABC.

items.title: G7 to hold emergency meeting on oil prices, Iran names Khamenei's son supreme leader
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he has been talking with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who will have input on when to end the war with Iran.

items.title: In defying Trump, Iran's mysterious new leader is a marked man
items.description: US President Donald Trump said the worst-case scenario in Iran would be if Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's successor were "as bad as the previous person". In many ways, the appointment of his son, Mojtaba Khamenei, delivers him that very outcome.

items.title: The signs Hegseth's wartime bravado isn't convincing Americans
items.description: The US administration's unapologetic stance on the war has come with a lot of bravado, but there are signs the American public is not convinced.

items.title: Labor MP warns linking Israeli government to antisemitism is 'dangerous'
items.description: Josh Burns also acknowledged the government had not always acted fast enough to deal with antisemitism and said it was necessary to be "humble" in the wake of the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: 'Every war game': The problem with the US strategy in Iran
items.description: A former top US diplomat says her country's efforts to topple Iran's leadership risks destabilising the region and strengthening the nation's Revolutionary Guard.

items.title: Bondi Beach gunman seeks to suppress family's identity over safety concerns
items.description: Naveed Akram faces 59 charges, including 15 counts of murder and one of committing a terrorist attack, over the shooting on December 14.

items.title: Bali scooter crash leaves 'vibrant' mum fighting for life
items.description: A mother of two from the NSW Central Coast was holidaying in Bali with her girlfriends when she was hit by a truck while riding a scooter.

items.title: Australians in Bali sentenced for murder of Melbourne father
items.description: An Indonesian court has jailed two Australian men for 16 years for the murder of Zivan Radmanovic, 32, in June last year.

items.title: Katherine locals survey flood damage as volunteers rally to help
items.description: An "army" of volunteers has hit the streets of Katherine to help residents worst affected by the weekend's flooding, as they survey the damage from near-record river rises.

items.title: NAB warns rising petrol prices could drive inflation above 5 per cent
items.description: More pain could be coming from motorists if economists' predictions about the impact of rising fuel prices on inflation prove correct.

items.title: Age verification for R-rated games and websites raises privacy concerns
items.description: New online safety codes requiring R-rated games and websites to verify their users' ages come into effect, prompting concerns about online privacy.

items.title: Farmers warn grocery prices could rise as war sparks fuel supply fears
items.description: Farmers say consumers could soon feel the impact of fuel shortages and soaring prices at the checkout, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global supply chains.

items.title: Ex-Liberal MP cleared of majority of charges in sexual assault trial
items.description: A jury has cleared former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon of the majority of charges he faced over the alleged sexual assault of a 13-year-old boy he met through a hook-up app in 2017.

items.title: A career break gave one woman a 'safety net' to return to her job
items.description: Whether it’s for a holiday, additional study or a exploring a new field of work, experts say a career break can have many benefits.

items.title: What happens to a severely disabled child when a mother's love is gone?
items.description: Deirdre Croft has dedicated 45 years to caring and advocating for her intellectually disabled son, Richard. Each passing day brings more pressure to secure his future when she's gone.

items.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle to visit Australia next month
items.description: The visit will mark seven years since they last touched down in the country for their successful tour as the newlywed Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

items.title: Dons coach leaves Merrett to prepare his way for Hawks
items.description: Former Essendon captain Zach Merrett is the centre of attention in the build-up to a round-one blockbuster against the club he attempted to join in the off-season.

items.title: Are the US-Israeli strikes on Iran legal?
items.description: International law bans countries from using force against each other, with a few exceptions. The US and Israel have been trying to argue their operations against Iran are in self-defence.  Part of that argument is their decades-long fear that Tehran is developing a nuclear weapon. So do those self-defence arguments stack up? And if they don’t, what happens next?

items.title: Supply lines open after food shortage, amid major Katherine flooding
items.description: While Katherine remains under an emergency flood warning, water levels are now receding and food supply lines are opening up.

items.title: Climbers sustain injuries after falling at Bluff Knoll while tethered together
items.description: Two climbers injured in a fall on Bluff Knoll, in WA's Great Southern, are winched off the mountain by helicopter and taken to Albany for treatment.

items.title: Frustrated Matildas exposed by South Korea but prepared for the long road at Asian Cup
items.description: In the moments that mattered, the Matildas lacked composure, while South Korea made them pay. They'll now have to do it the hard way if they're going to go all the way at the Women's Asian Cup.

items.title: Australian business owners in Dubai 'staying put'
items.description: Escalating geopolitical tensions mean Australians operating businesses in the Middle East have had to make quick changes to their daily operations.

items.title: The tormented future facing Ukraine's children after four years of war
items.description: Ukraine's children have grown up amid four years of Vladimir Putin's war. Some who survived have revealed their sadness, hope, torment and aspirations.
